label: Bible Study
prompt: Take therefore no thought for the _____: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.
verse: Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.
note: 'Morrow' is KJV for tomorrow — and tomorrow, Jesus says, can do its own worrying.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: And it shall come to pass, that before they call, I will _____; and while they are yet speaking, I will hear.
verse: And it shall come to pass, that before they call, I will answer; and while they are yet speaking, I will hear.
note: Before they call, I will answer — God's reply is on the way before the prayer is finished.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And he was in the hinder part of the ship, asleep on a _____: and they awake him, and say unto him, Master, carest thou not that we perish?
verse: And he was in the hinder part of the ship, asleep on a pillow: and they awake him, and say unto him, Master, carest thou not that we perish?
note: Mid-storm, Jesus was asleep on a pillow in the back of the boat — only Mark mentions the pillow.

label: Deep Water
prompt: Then they that feared the LORD spake often one to another: and the LORD hearkened, and heard it, and a book of _____ was written before him for them that feared the LORD, and that thought upon his name.
verse: Then they that feared the LORD spake often one to another: and the LORD hearkened, and heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared the LORD, and that thought upon his name.
note: While cynics said serving God was pointless, the faithful kept talking — and heaven kept minutes.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: But put ye on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make not _____ for the flesh, to fulfil the lusts thereof.
verse: But put ye on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make not provision for the flesh, to fulfil the lusts thereof.
note: The passage that converted Augustine in a Milan garden in 386, after a voice said 'take up and read.'
